tb21_profile.skill: Reimplement a trained neural net's forward pass by hand from exported weights, decode a PNG into normalized pixels, and ship it as a compiled CLI binary with an exact argv/stdout contract
tb21_profile.domain: PyTorch/MNIST inference, JSON weight serialization, PNG image decoding, C/Go/Rust compilation and packaging into an executable
tb21_profile.task_form: implement-from-spec plus build/packaging: produce an artifact (binary + weights.json + prediction.txt) at exact paths

verifier_notes: Checked tests for model-training_20260617_051646_002 (strong, 5 tests / 3 pinned) and model-training_20260612_191200_002 (strong, 6 tests / 4 pinned) via work/verifier_strength.json; both genuinely pin numeric predictions, so the grades hold. tw_588262 (YOLOv4 inference on a real image) is the only TerminalWorld entry that is close in domain and it is FREE (0 substantive of its suite) - ranked in per_source, excluded from final_top10. task_003915_9cae8761 is graded weak (4 of 5 tests are file-exists); its one substantive test does check the prediction output, so it is usable but thin.

Deserialize an MNIST pickle and recover the 28x28 digit images; same MNIST data layout and pixel-array handling the CLI must get right.

Standalone C predictor invoked as `./xgb_predict model input.csv`, parsing a model dump and writing prediction.txt - same argv, artifact and output-file contract.
Reverse-engineer a custom binary weight format (magic, uint32/float32 LE) and implement LeakyReLU/softmax inference; same weights-file-to-forward-pass work, harder parsing.
Load model.pth against model.py and classify PNG test images against pinned labels; same image-in/class-out deployment with per-image ground truth.
Write a PNG decoder in C (chunks, CRC, zlib inflate, unfiltering) compiled with gcc - the hardest sub-problem of reading image.png inside a compiled cli_tool.
Reimplement a pure-NumPy network wired to loose .npy weight files, some of which are decoys; forces shape-driven identification of which weights belong where.
Decode input.png to BMP with only the Python stdlib; same no-library image decoding, no model component.
Repair a broken checkpoint (config and weights) until it loads and reproduces expected outputs; checkpoint-to-architecture reconciliation.
Prune and quantize a PyTorch MNIST model for edge deployment; same MNIST weights and deployment framing, different transformation.

Infer the MNIST architecture from a state dict and reimplement every op by hand with correct 0.1307/0.3081 normalization - the core of this task.
Recover a model from an out-of-band spec, implement inference in Go, compile to an exact executable path with a strict stdout format.
Standalone C predictor invoked as `./xgb_predict model input.csv` writing prediction.txt; identical argv-plus-output-file packaging.
Hand-coded C++ MLP forward pass parsing a weights file, compiled with -O3 and driven end to end by a script.
Parse a custom little-endian binary weight file and implement LeakyReLU/softmax inference; weight-format reading plus forward pass.
Load a PyTorch checkpoint against its model.py and classify PNG images against pinned per-image labels - image-in/class-out with real ground truth.
PNG decoder in C: chunks, CRC, inflate, unfiltering - the part of reading image.png inside a compiled binary that most solutions get wrong.
Forward pass computed by hand from W1/b1/W2/b2 in weights.json with explicit ReLU equations; the exact arithmetic cli_tool reproduces.
Rebuild a pure-NumPy network from loose .npy weight files containing decoys; shape-driven mapping of weights onto layers.

notes: CalibForge decisively beats the v1 pool here: it contains a near-isomorph (compile a C binary that reads exported weights and prints an MNIST-style class) plus a whole cluster of from-scratch PNG decoders in C, which is the sub-problem the v1 pool had nothing for. TMax contributes real compiled-inference tasks (Go/C++ CLI scorers) and is the only other corpus worth drawing from. Terminal-Lego is shallow here - StackOverflow Keras/TF demo scripts, mostly weak verifiers; its best entries teach forward-pass and PNG-to-array mechanics but at toy depth. TerminalWorld and Recursive-Task-Synthesis could not field 10 defensible candidates: RTS offers only the sds-mnist setup cluster (all `absent`, all env plumbing) and generic compile-a-binary chores, and TerminalWorld's one domain-close entry (tw_588262, YOLOv4 inference) is FREE. SWE-Smith/Rebench lose on task_form as expected; their honest contribution is PyTorch weight-init/shape debugging (fvcore, gpytorch) and Keras save/reload bugs.
